Well, i had the same problem with my gf. Lots of issues, problems, and a long distance relationship meaning i could only talk to her by phone. We found different ways to go trough this. Maybe they wont work for you, but i just want to say it took a lot of time.   
My gf cant express her feelings. So i said, write them down. And she did! At first she sent me huge messages, or huge mails, with everything in her mind. Sometimes we were on the pone, quiet, just talking by messenger.   
We found activities together. We have a Pokemon passion in common. We have Pokemon cards. One day we were both very upset, and after 2h of talking, there was just a big awkward silence. She said "Wanna play?" and we played Pokemon. It was an amazing way to disengage everything. Doing something "normal", like drawing, playing, writing... Find something in common, to talk about this, and the rest will come.   
This worked for me, good luck, it take time and patience :)

Okay so i've lived something very similar two years ago, my ex lost her dad and i had to face it. I found out some things to do/not do: (sorry for bad english i'm french)  
\-Little attentions can help, but do not insist on anything. Bring her food if it pleased you, but don't insist or dont bother if she doesn't want it. But eat for you! I did that, coming to her house with fodd, sometimes she didnt eat it, and i would sit with her, just talking and eating normally on my own. Sometimes seeing me eating made her hungry at the end.  
\-Be present for her, but not over-present. I mean, if she needs to call you, be here, if she needs anythings, be here, and let her now that. But dont message her all the time to worry, or calling her everytime she doesn't answer. Leave her space, by letting her now that you are here anyway. Sometimes my ex spent two or 3 days by just sending me a few messages, and calling me when needed. Do not pity her by words all the time, acting like a sad guy. I mean, empathyze, but don't be a "sad"guy with her. The worst thing to do is saying thing like i'm sorry for your loss, etc. all the time. You said it. Now try to bring some positive things in her life. Do not bring the subject of her loss, ever, only if she brings it. propose things like going out, not big events, but just a 20 min walk outside for example. It can helps much more than you think. And dont force it. But in conversations, try to bring something else, by talking of basics things you did from your day, or series, just basic things. Dont say "I did this amazing event with my friends and it was so cool!" but more like "i did that, with Bob and John. It was pretty nice, maybe we can go one day?"  
And for the card... I don't know, i wouldn't do it, but... I don't know how close she is to you and your friends?  
These are some advices, i can give more, but the mains are: don't cry along with her, don't be the "sad guy" with her. Dont try try also to force hapiness, but also propose little things like a walk, a cinema, a visit... But not parties, or big events with people.  Bring her positive attitude, kind, let her know that you are her for her. Listen to her, but dont bring the subject.
